home.hero_subtitle: An interactive educational platform for understanding how the MD5 hash and its keyed cousin HMAC-MD5 work. Type your text, pick a depth, watch bits turn into a fingerprint.
home.feature_1_desc: Every one of the 64 per-block operations. Every padding bit. Every XOR in HMAC. Nothing hidden.
home.feature_2_desc: Big picture, per-round, or full bit-level — switch on the fly.
home.feature_3_desc: Supply a key and we swap to HMAC-MD5 automatically. Two MD5 passes, ipad/opad XOR included.
home.feature_4_desc: Difficulty-graded tasks, scoring, and progress — delivered by a typed backend API.
home.algo_desc: MD5 (Message Digest 5) was designed by Ron Rivest in 1991. It takes an arbitrary-length message and returns a 128-bit fingerprint. It's considered cryptographically broken today (collisions are trivial), but it's an excellent teaching example: every major idea from the hash-function family is here — padding, 512-bit blocks, Merkle-Damgård construction, four rounds with four distinct non-linear functions.

visualizer.input_text_placeholder: Type anything, e.g. 'The quick brown fox…'

avalanche.title: Avalanche effect
avalanche.desc: Flip a single input bit — the hash is completely different. That's what makes a hash a hash.

visualizer.empty_state_desc: Type some text (and optionally a key), pick a depth, and press Hash.

education.title: Practice tasks
education.subtitle: Solve MD5 / HMAC-MD5 problems, earn points, track progress.
education.task_detail_empty: Pick a task on the left to begin.

about.title: About
about.goal_desc: Educational platform for cryptographic primitives. We picked MD5 + HMAC-MD5 as a representative Merkle-Damgård hash.
